facts.text: On this date in 1945, Japan announced its surrender, ending WWII — yet the official peace treaty with Russia was never signed. Japan and Russia remain technically without one to this day.
On August 14, 1959, the Pacific island of Vanuatu did not exist as a concept. It gained independence in 1980 speaking four official languages across a chain of 80 islands smaller than Connecticut.
Monaco is smaller than Central Park, yet it has the world's highest GDP per capita and a longer life expectancy than any country on Earth.
More people live within a 25-mile radius of Manila than in the entire country of Australia.
The city of Chongqing, China, has more residents than Canada. Most people outside Asia have never heard of it.
On Aug 14, 1971, Nixon's advisors met at Camp David to end the gold standard. Three days later, the dollar was unmoored from gold forever — the most consequential weekend in modern financial history.
On Aug 14, 1945, Japan surrendered. U.S. stock markets surged so violently that trading had to be halted — the Dow's single-day gain that week remains one of the largest in its history.
The NYSE was once fined $1.65 billion in a single settlement. The acquirer: itself — the NYSE paid to acquire Euronext in 2006, briefly making it the first transatlantic stock exchange.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion in a single day — enough to buy every NFL franchise, every NBA franchise, and still have change left over.
The entire global bond market is roughly $130 trillion — about 1.3x the size of world GDP. Most people invest in stocks. Professionals mostly live in bonds.

On this day in 1888, Oberlin College granted the first PhD to a Black American — but the human brain processing that historical fact right now contains more synaptic connections than there are stars in the Milky Way.
Your skeleton is not a static scaffold. Every decade, your entire bone mass is silently replaced, atom by atom, through a process called remodeling.
On August 14, 1959, Explorer 6 captured the first photograph of Earth from orbit — revealing a pale smear that confirmed we live on a sphere surrounded by the void.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
The mantis shrimp sees with 16 types of color receptors — four times more than humans — yet research suggests it processes color worse than we do, trading perception for raw speed.
On this day in 1945, Japan announced its surrender — but fighting continued in some Pacific outposts for days, and one soldier, Hiroo Onoda, kept fighting until 1974.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford dates to 1096; Tenochtitlán wasn't founded until 1325.
On this day in 1935, FDR signed Social Security into law — a program now older than the microwave oven, the Slinky, and the bikini.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, and a full 146 years before the World Wide Web.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable in one word to English, it folds nostalgia, grief, and belonging into a single breath.
On this day in 1888, an patent was filed for the first commercially viable adding machine by William Burroughs — whose grandson would later coin the word 'heavy metal' for a novel.
Petrichor (n.): the scent of rain on dry earth. Named in 1964 by Australian scientists Bear and Thomas, from Greek petra (stone) and ichor, the fluid said to flow in gods' veins.
On August 14, 1945, Japan announced surrender — and the word 'VJ Day' entered English instantly, a portmanteau born from relief so vast it needed coining before the ink was dry.

On this date in 2017, Bitcoin's SegWit upgrade activated at block 481,824 — ending a years-long civil war between miners and developers over block size, and quietly enabling the Lightning Network to exist.
On August 14, 2020, Yam Finance collapsed within 35 hours of launch after a rebase bug minted uncontrolled governance tokens, destroying $750M in locked value before a single audit was completed.
Ethereum's gas limit is not set by code — it's a miner (now validator) vote each block, nudged ±0.1% per block, meaning network throughput is a rolling social consensus, not a protocol constant.

The FBI wallet holding Bitcoin seized from Silk Road in 2013 briefly made the U.S. government one of the largest single BTC holders on earth, with over 144,000 coins — more than many sovereign funds hold today.

Bitcoin's difficulty adjustment recalculates every 2,016 blocks, a number chosen so that at the original 10-minute target it resets almost exactly every two weeks — an elegant clock baked into the protocol's bones.

On this date in 2006, Geoffrey Hinton and colleagues published the paper that revived deep learning by showing deep belief nets could be pre-trained layer by layer — ending a decade of neural network winter.

On this date in 2012, ImageNet's competition closed submissions. AlexNet's winning entry wouldn't be public for weeks, but the GPU-trained network had already halved the error rate no one thought was beatable.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed around 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — roughly the annual usage of 4,500 American homes, spent entirely before a single user query was answered.

AlphaFold2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins, covering nearly every catalogued organism on Earth. The entire dataset was released freely in 2022, arguably the largest single donation to biology in history.

The first neural network to beat a human at Go, AlphaGo, did so in 2016 using policy and value networks trained on 30 million human moves — then immediately became obsolete when AlphaGo Zero learned from zero human data and crushed it.
